parameters.name: deliveredAfter
parameters.description:
Delivery-date range, filtering `Project.deliveryEnabledAt`.

IMPORTANT: `deliveryEnabledAt` is the LATEST delivery — it is overwritten
every time the project is delivered again (revision re-deliveries,
re-sends), so this filter means "most recently delivered in this range",
not "was ever delivered in this range". A project delivered in March and
re-delivered in May does NOT match a March range.

A bare `YYYY-MM-DD` covers the whole UTC day on both ends, so
after = before = one day returns that day's deliveries.

parameters.name: firstDeliveredAfter
parameters.description:
FIRST-delivery range, filtering `Project.firstDeliveredAt` — written once,
the first time the job was delivered, and never overwritten.

This is the counterpart to deliveredAfter/deliveredBefore above, which read
`deliveryEnabledAt` (the LATEST delivery). Both exist because both questions
are real and they give different answers whenever a job is re-delivered:
"what did we deliver in March" wants the first delivery, "what is live /
most recently delivered" wants the latest. A job first delivered in March
and re-delivered in July is in a March range here, and in a July range
there.

Same bare-date semantics as every other range: a `YYYY-MM-DD` covers the
whole UTC day on both ends, so after = before = one day returns that day.

The column is NULL for rows delivered before it existed, so this range only
sees deliveries actually on record — it never infers one from
`deliveryEnabledAt`, which would re-import exactly the ambiguity it exists
to remove.

parameters.name: paymentStatus
parameters.description: Payment status filter: 'paid' → paidAt set; 'unpaid' → paidAt null.

parameters.name: technicianId
parameters.description:
Single technician (saved views + deep links keep sending this). Merged
server-side with `technicianIds`, deduped — the two are one filter.

parameters.name: technicianIds
parameters.description:
Multi-select technicians. Matches a person assigned ANYWHERE on the
project: the legacy `Project.technicianId` scalar, the ProjectTechnician
join, a shoot's own technician, or a shoot's crew.

parameters.name: technicianMatch
parameters.description:
How to combine `technicianIds`:
  - 'any' (default) → the project has at least one of them assigned
  - 'all'           → EVERY selected person is assigned somewhere on the
                      project. Deliberately not "all on the same shoot" —
                      crews are per-visit, and the useful question when
                      auditing a job is who worked it at all.

parameters.name: crewSize
parameters.description:
Shoot-crew size — how many DISTINCT technicians are staffed on the job,
counted across all four places one can be attached (the project scalar,
ProjectTechnician, a LIVE shoot's own technician, and that shoot's crew).

  'solo' | '1'              → exactly one technician
  'crew' | 'team' | 'multi' → two or more
  'N' | 'N+' (N = 1..50)    → N or more
  '' (a cleared select)     → no filter

Unassigned jobs (0 technicians) match NO crew size — that question is
`technicianAssigned=false`.

The pattern deliberately mirrors ProjectsService.parseCrewSizeFilter, which
owns this vocabulary: `whitelist: true` strips anything this DTO does not
declare, so a value the parser understands but this regex rejects would be
unreachable code, while anything this lets through that the parser does not
accept (N outside 1..50) gets a 400 from the parser itself. Keep the two in
step.

NOT applied by buildProjectFilters. Prisma cannot express a to-many
cardinality in `where` (no `_count`, no self-correlation), so this resolves
through a pre-query that is AND-ed onto the clause — and it has to happen on
the list, the ids ("select all") AND the metrics query, or the chip count
disagrees with the rows beneath it. ProjectsService.applyCrewSizeFilter is
the one place that does it, and every project-list surface routes through
it.

parameters.name: serviceAreaIds
parameters.description:
Service-area coverage, matched against the DERIVED
`Project.resolvedServiceAreaId` (where the property falls TODAY, re-derived
from lat/lng against the org's current areas) plus two sentinels for the
states that have no id:
  - '__outside__' → placed, and inside no area
  - '__unknown__' → could not be placed at all (no usable coordinates)
They are not uuids, so they cannot collide with a real area id. See
SERVICE_AREA_OUTSIDE / SERVICE_AREA_UNKNOWN in common/utils/filter-builder.

This filter existed as a correct predicate for a while but was withheld
from the DTO, because it pointed at the frozen `Project.serviceAreaId` —
a booking-time BILLING snapshot that InvoicesService reads to choose
per-area pricing, and that carries a value on ~no rows (0 of 3218 on dev).
Filtering it matched nothing, and backfilling it would have changed what
un-invoiced jobs cost. The derived column exists so filtering can be right
without money moving; the frozen column stays frozen.

'__unknown__' is always trustworthy. '__outside__' is not: NULL covers both
"placed, matched nothing" and "nothing was derived", so it needs the
backfill to have run AND the org to have active coordinate-based coverage
(an org with name-based areas only resolves nothing, and every project would
read as outside). See the predicate comment in buildProjectFilters.

parameters.name: travelFeeZoneIds
parameters.description:
Travel-fee zone, matched against the DERIVED
`Project.resolvedTravelFeeZoneId`. Zones are the concentric distance bands
configured inside each service area (they live only in the
`Organization.serviceArea` JSON — there is no zone table), so a zone id is
only meaningful next to its area; pair this with `serviceAreaIds`.

Withheld until now for the same reason as serviceAreaIds: the
`Project.travelFee*` columns are the immutable billing snapshot, frozen so
that moving a zone boundary can never rewrite a historical invoice, and 0%
populated. "Which zone is this property in today" is a different question,
and it gets its own derived column.

parameters.name: includeArchived
parameters.description:
When true, archived projects are included in the result. Defaults to
false (archived projects are hidden). Only the deep "Archived Orders"
settings page should pass true.

parameters.name: archivedOnly
parameters.description:
When true, returns ONLY archived orders — the projects-page "Archived"
filter. Distinct from includeArchived (which returns both). Also opts out
of the default cancelled-exclusion since archived orders are cancelled.

parameters.name: workspaceOrgId
parameters.description:
For customer-side viewers (resolveHubViewer: an AGENT, or anyone with team
visibility standing): narrows the cross-org "my projects" list to one
vendor. THE rule is `resolveWorkspaceScopeOrgId`
(common/customer-visibility.util.ts), in order:
- A token bound to a vendor (`wl`) is forced to that vendor, whatever is
  sent here.
- Absent, or ANY personal org (the caller's own included): every vendor —
  the personal workspace is the "all my orders" view.
- A non-personal org the caller has a relation with (a customer record, an
  active share on one of its orders, or team-administrator reach into it):
  that vendor only.
- Anything else: ignored (every vendor).

parameters.name: budgetMinCents
parameters.description:
Budget bounds, in cents, matched against the job's own range.

parameters.name: mine
parameters.description:
Narrow the list to work this caller is actually part of: jobs they posted,
or jobs where a slot is assigned to them.

── WHY THIS EXISTS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

`listJobs` is the PUBLIC feed — by design it returns every job that is not
a targeted RFQ, because browsing other people's open jobs is the point of a
marketplace. The provider's "Active Jobs" screen called that same endpoint
with nothing but a status filter, so a page titled as the caller's own work
listed everybody's: on this clone, 17 jobs where 6 were theirs, each one
carrying the agent's name, the budget, the escrow amount and the review
text both parties left each other.

Filtered HERE rather than in the screen, because a client-side filter would
still have put all of it on the wire.

Posted-OR-assigned rather than assigned-only: the same screen is reachable
by an agent, and their own jobs are theirs to see either way.

parameters.name: withinMyServiceArea
parameters.description:
Only jobs inside the CALLER'S OWN service circle (their provider profile's
centre + `serviceRadiusKm`). Jobs with no coordinates are left out under
this flag.

A caller with no circle gets the flag IGNORED, not an empty feed: "nothing
near you" would be a lie told to somebody who simply has not picked an
area yet. Applied in the database, so `total` is exact.

parameters.name: sortBy
parameters.description:
`(sortBy, sortOrder)` come from `PaginationDto`, redeclared here ONLY to
narrow `sortBy` to the columns this list can actually order by — the base
is an open `string`, and an unvalidated column name reaching Prisma's
`orderBy` is not something to hand a caller.

`declare` because the base already defines them; a plain redeclaration
shadows the decorated property and silently drops its validation.

SERVER-SIDE, and for a sharper reason than the filters: sorting one page of
twenty is not sorting. "Highest budget" returned the highest of whichever
twenty jobs the server happened to send — the wrong answer the moment a
twenty-first exists, and it looks right because the page IS correctly
ordered within itself.

get.summary:
Everything needed to review and approve a run honestly, in one request:
the run (with an INCLUSIVE period label — `periodEnd` is stored exclusive),
items with sources and adjustments, human labels for the projects behind each
line, the claims the run holds, run-level totals including adjustments, and
the review counters (pending / approved / excluded / needs-attention,
canFinalize, canExport).

`GET :id/items` alone returned bare UUIDs for project and visit, so a reviewer
had no address, client or job to judge against — and the run total was never
shown on the screen that finalizes it.

── WHAT APPLYING TODAY'S INCENTIVE RULES WOULD DO, BEFORE ANYBODY CLICKS ──

Same URL as the POST, deliberately: GET asks, POST acts, and a UI that can
state the blast radius reads the identical address it is about to write to.

`payroll.read`, because it reads and writes nothing. It returns the org-wide
scope of the change as data (`scope: 'ORGANIZATION'`), how many payees and
lines on THIS run would be paid and how much per currency, how many
approvals the recompute would reset, what employees are structurally
withheld from it, and which OTHER runs sit in the window — because an
incentive rule belongs to the organization, not to the payee whose screen
this was opened from, and nobody should learn that after the fact.

post.summary:
MAKE THE BACKTRACED AMOUNTS REAL: put the rules in force over the work they
were written for, through the effective-dating engine, and recompute.

Writes no money. It writes incentive-rule predecessors — the same
`OrgIncentiveRule` versioning every bonus already goes through — and then
runs the ordinary recompute, which prices the run from
`incentiveRulesInForceAt` + `evaluateIncentive` exactly as it always does.
There is no second grant path and no hand-typed figure.

Refused on a FINALIZED or EXPORTED run (un-finalize first — that work is
claimed), while a run is COMPUTING, and when today's rules already apply.

── THE FOUR VERBS AN ADJUSTMENT NEEDS, AND WHERE EACH ONE LIVES ───────────

  ADD     POST   /payroll/items/:id/adjustments        (this route)
  BULK    POST   /payroll/runs/:id/adjustments/bulk    — N lines, N rows,
                                                         one `batchId`
  TWEAK   PATCH  /payroll/adjustments/:adjustmentId
  REMOVE  DELETE /payroll/adjustments/:adjustmentId

REMOVING A LINE is not a fifth route: it is `kind: 'LINE_REMOVAL'` on ADD or
BULK, whose cents are DERIVED from the line rather than typed. It is a
different STATEMENT from a delta, not a different verb — and putting it on
the same routes is what stops "removed" and "adjusted to zero" becoming two
records of one decision. Deleting the removal is what puts the line back.

Response bodies: ADD returns `{ adjustmentCents, totalCents }` — byte-
identical to what it returned before line scoping, so existing callers are
untouched. Everything else a reader needs about an adjustment (its id, kind,
reason, provenance, batch and the line it names) comes from the run review's
`adjustmentLedger`, which is the ONE read model for it.

Adjust MANY lines in one request — across several payees if need be.

Writes ONE `PayrollAdjustment` PER LINE, never one row for the batch: a
single row covering fourteen lines is the same opaque lump this whole change
exists to delete, only bigger, and undoing one of the fourteen would mean
rewriting the other thirteen. The shared `batchId` in the response is what
still lets a reader say "these fourteen were done together".

Scoped to the RUN and not to an item, because a batch legitimately spans
payees — and scoping it here is what makes "these pay lines are not on this
run" checkable in one place.

parameters.name: includeUnappliedRules
parameters.description:
── THE OVERRIDE. OFF BY DEFAULT, AND DELIBERATE WHEN IT IS ON ────────────

Include what today's incentive rules would award on this payee's completions
but the run has NOT applied, as ordinary money in the `incentive` column and
in `total`.

THE DEFAULT PATH IS NOT THIS FLAG. It is `POST
/payroll/runs/:id/apply-todays-rules`, which backdates the rules through the
effective-dating engine and recomputes the run, so the run's own figure and
the file agree and there is no gap for anybody to reconcile later. This flag
exists for when that is not wanted — the run is left untouched and the file
carries the money anyway.

THE FILE DOES NOT ANNOUNCE IT, and that is a decision rather than an
oversight: this file is a payment instruction, the amounts on it are the
amounts being paid, and a column of caveats on a document a bookkeeper
imports wholesale would compete with a `total` that is unambiguous. THE
PLATFORM announces it instead — the per-payee export audit entry records
that the file included un-applied amounts and exactly how many cents, so the
difference between this file and the run is reconstructable from the record
even though it is invisible on the page.

ONLY EVER UPWARDS. If today's rules would award LESS than the run committed
to (a rule was retired since the work), the run's figure stands: a payment
instruction that quietly pays somebody less than the run says they are owed
is a short payment, and no flag on a download should be able to cause one.

parameters.description:
Where each shoot's drive is measured from.

    technician's previous shoot on the same org-local day is measured from
    that previous property; everything else still starts at home, and only
    the last shoot of the day carries a drive home. It is the default
    because it is what the day the technician is actually booked into
    costs, which is the question an owner opens this panel to ask.
  HOME_BASE — every shoot is a fresh round trip from the assigned
    technician's home base. The conservative upper bound: it never credits
    this project with a drive another job paid for.
  RECORDED_TRIP — each shoot is MEASURED from where the technician's device
    said they set off (`ProjectTracking.startLatitude/startLongitude`), with
    CHAINED as the fall-back for any shoot that has no usable fix. Accepted
    unconditionally rather than 400'd when no trip exists: the response
    carries `recordedTripModeAvailable` so the client can grey the option
    out, and a mode that rejected the request would leave a client that
    asked for it stuck on an error screen instead of on the numbers.

Optional: an absent param must mean "the default", not a 400, because the
page loads before the operator has touched the toggle.

THE DEFAULT IS APPLIED IN `ProjectCostEstimateController`, and it has to
stay equal to the mode `ProjectCostEstimateTab` opens on. If those two ever
disagree, the panel's first paint and its first refetch show different
money for the same project.

parameters.name: invoiceId
parameters.description:
Scope the REVENUE half of this estimate to ONE invoice on the project.

Absent means the whole order, which is what the panel asked for before the
per-invoice view existed and what every non-invoice caller still asks for.

## Why this param exists

Project-scoped revenue is the SUM of every invoice on the project. On a
CA$299.99 job with three drafts on it the panel reported CA$899.97 of revenue
and an 87.5% margin computed from it. The screen is now reached from an
invoice and states which one.

## Read the guard notes before adding another param

The global `ValidationPipe` runs `whitelist: true` AND
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so a key not declared on this class 400s the
whole request rather than being ignored. The frontend must send exactly
`invoiceId`.

`@IsString` rather than `@IsUUID`: `Invoice.id` defaults to `uuid()` today,
but imported and migrated rows are not guaranteed to have been minted by that
default, and a validator that 400s a real invoice id is worse than one that
lets a bad id reach a WHERE clause that will simply not match. The id is only
ever used inside `findMany({ where: { projectId, orgId, ... } })` and compared
in memory — it reaches no raw SQL — and a miss is a 404, so the length cap is
about bounding the payload, not about safety.

x-api-key.name: x-api-key
x-api-key.description: Organization API key. The organization is derived from the key, so x-org-id is not required and is ignored if sent. Scoped: READ covers safe methods, WRITE implies READ, ADMIN covers everything, BULK_IMPORT and WEBHOOKS are narrow.

plan.description:
Which plan to subscribe to. Omitted means ENTERPRISE, the only plan this
route offered before TEAM existed.

interval.description:
Billing interval. Only meaningful for TEAM, which is sold at two prices;
ENTERPRISE has a single configured price and ignores this.

category.description:
Raw backend category for this notification's type. Lets clients group /
 filter the inbox without re-deriving the taxonomy from the type.

assignedProjects.description: Preview of the projects in the batch (capped server-side, newest first).

senderName.description:
Display name of the user who sent the message — used by the
 inbox row to surface "From <senderName>" instead of a generic
 "New message" headline.

mentioned.description:
True when THIS recipient was @mentioned in the message body. Lets clients
 render "<senderName> mentioned you" and keep the row out of the
 "N new messages" per-project rollup — an unmissable direct callout rather
 than one more line in the chat firehose.

messageId.description:
The chat message this notification is about. Needed to deep-link to the
 specific message (scroll/highlight), not just the project's chat tab.

ratingMediaType.description: Media-type CODE, set only for a per-media-type EDITOR rating.

cartId.description:
For BOOKING_ABANDONED — the `PendingOrder.id` of the unfinished cart.

Flattened out of the payload rather than left in it for the same reason
`assignedCount` is: a client that reads only `projectId` renders this row
with a dead "View Project" button, because a PendingOrder has no Project by
construction. This id is the `?resume=` target the booking flow, the resume
screen and the checkout-cancel page already use — clients deep-link to
`/booking?resume=<cartId>` and must not invent a second address for it.

videoScriptSetId.description:
For VIDEO_SCRIPTS_READY — the `VideoScriptSet.id` this row announces.

`projectId` is present on this row too (the scripts belong to a listing),
so unlike `cartId` this is not what rescues the row from being untappable.
It is what makes the tap land on the RIGHT thing: a listing accumulates a
set per regeneration, and an agent who asked for a rewrite and then opened
a week-old notification must get the set that notification was about, not
whatever is newest. Flattened out of the payload for the same reason every
field above is — clients read the DTO, not the raw payload blob.

customerId.description:
CUSTOMER_EMAIL_UNDELIVERABLE: the OrganizationCustomer whose address can't
receive mail. The row's destination is that customer's page — the place
the address gets fixed — and for every org except the one whose send
bounced the row has no projectId at all, so this is what makes it tappable.

token.description: The push token. For platform=expo this is an ExponentPushToken[…] string. For platform=apns this is the hex-encoded APNs device token from application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:).

platform.description: Token format. 'expo' = Expo push service (RN app). 'apns' = direct APNs (SwiftUI app, see PRD §6.5). 'ios' / 'android' are accepted for backwards compatibility and treated as expo-format tokens.

bundleId.description: iOS CFBundleIdentifier (e.g. 'com.vremly.agent' or 'com.vremly.virtualxposure'). Required for platform=apns so the multi-tenant APNs sender picks the right auth key + team. Expo tokens omit it.

environment.description: APNs environment the device token was issued by: 'sandbox' for Debug-signed builds (aps-environment=development) or 'production' for App-Store / TestFlight builds. Apple's production gateway returns 200 OK for sandbox tokens but the push silently drops, so the dispatcher must send to the gateway that matches the token. Optional — when omitted the dispatcher falls back to its dual-gateway retry. Send "sandbox" from Swift Debug builds via `#if DEBUG`.

endpoint.description: The push service's delivery URL for this browser. THE identity of the subscription — the row is upserted on it. Must be https and must not resolve to an internal host (see isAcceptablePushEndpoint).

userAgent.description: Browser UA at registration. Display only; never routed on.

origin.description: The origin the service worker was registered from, e.g. "https://app.vremly.com" or a tenant's own domain. Required — a subscription with an unknown origin cannot be attributed to a tenant.

endpoint.description: The endpoint to stop sending to.

allDayFree.description: All-day entries the calendar publishes as FREE (public holidays).

allDayBusy.description: All-day entries the calendar publishes as BUSY (vacation / out-of-office).

tentative.description:
ALL-DAY entries the calendar publishes as TENTATIVE. A TIMED tentative
 entry always blocks and is deliberately not configurable — see
 classifyExternalEvent, whose all-day gate runs first.

accountType.description:
User-facing intent for the account.
Only AGENT and PROVIDER are user-facing in the UI.

whitelabelOrgId.description:
When the user signs up on a whitelabel custom domain, this is the
orgId of that company. The backend creates an OrganizationCustomer
record so the user lands in that company's customer portal.
When signing up from a whitelabel workspace URL, auto-associate with this org

orgId.description: Optional org ID for whitelabel branding on the OTP email

purpose.description:
Purpose the code is issued for. Scopes how it can later be redeemed:
'signup' (default) rejects already-registered emails; 'login_2fa',
'password_reset' and 'returning_customer_setup' allow them. A code minted
for one purpose cannot be redeemed by another flow.

bonusSpendCents.description:
GRANTED PROGRESS, in cents, as a delta against earned lifetime spend.
Positive grants, negative corrects, 0 removes. Deliberately NOT `@Min(0)`:
a negative grant is how an operator walks back progress handed out in
error. The effective figure is floored at zero where it is read.

tierOverrideSlug.description:
GRANTED TIER pin. Must be an ENABLED tier slug for this org — the service
checks that against LoyaltyTierConfig, because class-validator cannot know
one org's tier list. `null` removes the pin.

reason.description:
Required, and load-bearing rather than decorative: this changes the rate
the customer earns cashback at on every future order, and loyalty credit is
redeemable against an invoice. The service trims and re-checks it, because
a single space passes `@IsString()`.

customerId.description:
An existing OrganizationCustomer in the caller's org. The service re-binds
it to `orgId` before touching anything — a bare id would otherwise let one
org mint a loyalty account against another org's customer.

email.description:
Grant to an email address instead. A recipient with no account is a
FIRST-CLASS case, not an edge case: the service creates (or adopts) the
customer row, mints a pending CUSTOMER invitation so the notification email
has a real signup link, and the reward is waiting when they arrive.

customerName.description:
Display name for a brand-new customer row created by the email arm. Ignored
when the address already belongs to a customer — an existing person's name
is theirs, and a grant is not the place to rename them.

cents.description: discount_next_order_cents — flat cents off the next order.

addOnId.description: free_add_on — PackageAddOn.id. The service checks it belongs to this org.

packageId.description:
free_package — ServicePackage.id.

A free_package reward is 100% off THE MATCHING PACKAGE'S LINE in an order.
It is not, and must never become, a blanket free order: if the customer's
order does not contain this package, the reward is simply not applicable
and the checkout says so. That is why the id is required rather than
optional — an entitlement with no packageId cannot be matched to a line,
and "matches nothing" would have to be resolved either by refusing every
order or by discounting all of them.

config.description: perk_template — the template's own config blob, shape defined per template.

expiresAt.description:
Absolute expiry instant, ISO-8601. OPTIONAL — omitting both this and
`expiresAfterDays` means the reward never expires, which is a supported
outcome rather than a missing value.

expiresAfterDays.description: TTL in days from the moment of the grant. Mutually exclusive with `expiresAt`.

note.description:
Why this was granted. Not required — unlike a manual credit adjustment,
which moves money against a balance — but it is what the audit line reads
six months later, so the UI should ask for it.

displayName.description:
Override the auto-generated label ("Free Premium Package"). The default is
computed from the catalog at grant time and frozen onto the row, so a
renamed package never blanks a customer's pending reward.

referrerCustomerId.description: The customer who did the referring — must be a customer of THIS org.

refereeCustomerId.description: The customer who was referred — must be a customer of THIS org.

reason.description:
WHY this is being recorded. Required, because the whole point of the
MANUAL source is that a human vouched for something the platform did not
see — a row that says "manual" with no reason is an assertion with no
author's account of it.

`@MaxLength(500)` matches ATTRIBUTION_REASON_MAX in the web client
(apps/frontend/lib/referral-attribution.ts), which is itself the same limit
the loyalty manual-adjustment reason uses — one org-wide dialect for "why
did a human do this by hand". A client that counts to a different number
would let a coordinator type a reason the server then rejects.

Trimmed before validation so a whitespace-only string fails @MinLength
rather than being stored as a blank reason.

addOnQuantities.description: Layered add-on quantities; omitted means one. Picker items always bill once. Flat-rate items bill once; other values are normalized to 1–99.

priceByAreaCents.description: Per-service-area price overrides in cents, keyed by service-area id ({ [serviceAreaId]: cents }). Each area uses its own currency; areas not listed fall back to `price`.

cogsPerOrderCentsByMediaType.description: COST OF GOODS SOLD (optional) — the OUTSOURCED production cost of this package’s included items, in integer cents, keyed by media-type CODE ({ "PHOTO": 4500, "CUSTOM_TWILIGHT": 12000 }). PER ORDER, not per unit: nothing in the schema persists a per-item quantity, so a figure here is the whole outsourcing cost for that media type on ONE project. An ABSENT key means nobody has set a figure — the Cost & Profit screen reports that as unknown and never counts it as zero; an explicit 0 is a DELIBERATE zero (produced in-house) and is a known figure. Send null for a key to clear it back to unknown. Keys must be media-type codes this organization knows (GET /media-types) and values whole cents >= 0; anything else is rejected rather than silently dropped, because a silently-dropped cost is indistinguishable from "not set". Denominated in the package currency. Excludes technician labour, which is computed separately from real pay rates.

mediaTypes.description: Included media types, as media-type CODES (e.g. "PHOTO", "VIDEO", or a custom "CUSTOM_TWILIGHT"). Call GET /media-types for this organization's codes — the valid set is per-organization, so this is deliberately not a closed enum.

includedAddOnIds.description: Money Model v3 — explicit IDs of PackageAddOn rows that this pre-built package "includes" for bundle-detection. When the Build-Your-Own picker selection is a superset of this list, the booking flow surfaces a "switch to bundle and save $X" callout. See docs/money-model-v3-design.md.

recommendedAddOnIds.description: Add-on IDs the company chose to upsell for this package — surfaced as "Recommended" (badge + top-sort) in the booking flow add-on step.

requiredKitId.description: P2 — id of the gear Kit this package requires on site. Seeded onto Project.requiredKitId when a booking selects this package, so the assignment UI can surface tech-readiness. Null/omitted = no specific kit required.

requiredCertLevelId.description: id of the CertificationLevel a technician must hold (PASSED, non-expired) to serve this package. Null/omitted = no certification required.

priceByAreaCents.description: Per-service-area price overrides in cents, keyed by service-area id ({ [serviceAreaId]: cents }). Each area uses its own currency; areas not listed fall back to `price`.

cogsPerOrderCentsByMediaType.description: COST OF GOODS SOLD (optional) — outsourced production cost per included media type, in integer cents, keyed by media-type CODE ({ "PHOTO": 4500, "CUSTOM_TWILIGHT": 12000 }). PER ORDER, not per unit. REPLACES the stored map wholesale, so send every entry you want kept; omit the field entirely to leave it unchanged, send {} to clear every figure, or send null for a single key to clear just that one. An absent key = nobody set a figure (reported as unknown, never zero); an explicit 0 = a deliberate zero (produced in-house) and is a known figure. Keys must be media-type codes this organization knows (GET /media-types) and values whole cents >= 0; anything else is rejected rather than silently dropped. Denominated in the package currency. Excludes technician labour.

mediaTypes.description: Included media types, as media-type CODES (e.g. "PHOTO", "VIDEO", or a custom "CUSTOM_TWILIGHT"). Call GET /media-types for this organization's codes — the valid set is per-organization, so this is deliberately not a closed enum.

questionSetIds.description: IDs of BookingQuestionSet rows to apply when this package is selected. Pass empty array to clear.

includedAddOnIds.description: Money Model v3 — explicit IDs of PackageAddOn rows that this pre-built package "includes" for bundle-detection. When the Build-Your-Own picker selection is a superset of this list, the booking flow surfaces a "switch to bundle and save $X" callout. Pass empty array to clear. See docs/money-model-v3-design.md.

recommendedAddOnIds.description: Add-on IDs the company chose to upsell for this package — surfaced as "Recommended" (badge + top-sort) in the booking flow add-on step.

requiredKitId.description: P2 — id of the gear Kit this package requires on site. Pass null to clear. Seeded onto Project.requiredKitId when a booking selects this package.

requiredCertLevelId.description: id of the CertificationLevel a technician must hold (PASSED, non-expired) to serve this package. Pass null to clear. Null/omitted = no certification required.

priceByAreaCents.description: Per-service-area price overrides in cents, keyed by service-area id ({ [serviceAreaId]: cents }). Each area uses its own currency; areas not listed fall back to `price`.

cogsPerOrderCents.description: COST OF GOODS SOLD (optional) — the OUTSOURCED production cost of this add-on, in integer cents, PER ORDER (not per unit: nothing persists a per-item quantity, so this is the whole outsourcing cost for this add-on on ONE project). Omit to leave unchanged; send null to state that no outsourcing cost is known, which CLEARS any existing figure. null and 0 are different facts and are treated differently downstream: null = nobody has set it, which the Cost & Profit screen reports as unknown and refuses to count as zero; 0 = a deliberate zero (produced in-house), a known figure that does not flag. Denominated in the add-on currency. Excludes technician labour, which is computed separately from real pay rates.

mediaTypes.description: Included media types, as media-type CODES (e.g. "PHOTO", "VIDEO", or a custom "CUSTOM_TWILIGHT"). Call GET /media-types for this organization's codes — the valid set is per-organization, so this is deliberately not a closed enum.

bundledPriceCents.description: Discounted price (in cents) when this add-on is bundled with a matching package. Falls back to `price` when omitted.

body.description:
The note. "The second one is too salesy", "it's a townhouse, not a condo",
"the seller called and wants the garage mentioned".

REQUIRED, unlike `GenerateVideoScriptsDto.feedback`, and that difference is
the whole point of the route: generating without notes is a legitimate
thing for the company to do, whereas submitting an EMPTY note is a row that
says nothing, notifies the company for nothing, and then feeds a blank line
into the model's prompt. `MinLength(1)` runs after class-validator has the
raw string, so a body of only whitespace still gets through here — the
service trims and refuses it, which is the one check that has to live where
every present and future caller passes.

The 2000-character cap matches the generate route's, and for the same
reason: this text goes STRAIGHT INTO AN LLM PROMPT, and the cap is the only
thing between a paste-bomb and the token bill. Notes ACCUMULATE now — a
generation composes every unconsumed one — so the cap is per note and the
service caps the composed total as well.

this DTO backs PATCH /users/me and the admin-facing UpdateUserDto
deliberately does NOT carry it, so an org owner cannot flip a colleague's
or a customer's sharing preference for them.

MUST be declared here. main.ts runs the ValidationPipe with `whitelist:
true` AND `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an undeclared field is not
dropped: the whole request is rejected with a 400 and the profile save
fails.

org owner cannot write a colleague's or customer's birthday.

Send all three as `null` to clear it.

NOTE the decorator asymmetry, which is intentional:
 - `birthdayMonth` carries the cross-field @Validate and NO @IsOptional, so

 - `birthdayDay` / `birthdayYear` carry @IsOptional @IsInt purely so a

editorIds.description:

COMBINES WITH {@link editorId} AS A UNION, DE-DUPLICATED, ORDER PRESERVED,
`editorId` FIRST — the rule lives in one place,
`projects/booking-editors.util.resolveBookingEditorIds`, whose header
states why. The resolved element 0 becomes the legacy `Project.editorId`

create, the same failure a bad `editorId` has always produced.

estimatedDuration.description:
Total shoot length in minutes for the initial appointment, as computed by
the create form (package + add-ons + any manually-added extra time).

ADVISORY, NEVER AUTHORITATIVE. The server resolves the package + add-ons
itself and that is the contract; this number is honoured only when it
EXCEEDS that resolved length — the form's "Add extra time" control is
strictly additive and is the only thing that produces such a number — and is
then recorded as an explicit MANUAL override attributed to the caller. An
equal or SHORTER number never overrules the package: no client can express a
deliberate shortening at booking, so a short number is a stale one.

When the catalogue carries no duration at all, this number is honoured ONLY
if the caller also sets {@link estimatedDurationIsManual}. Otherwise it is
ignored and the shoot is left with no contracted length, which keeps the
payroll flag alive. See `shoot-duration.util.decideBookingDuration`.

estimatedDurationIsManual.description:
"A human typed `estimatedDuration` into an otherwise-empty field."

The ONLY thing that lets a client-supplied number establish a length when
the catalogue is silent. It exists because the number alone cannot carry its
own provenance: every client used to send a FABRICATED value here — the
staff form pre-filled 120 and snapped back to 120 when cleared, the agent
flow held a `useState(120)` nothing ever updated — and the backend recorded
those as `contractedDurationSource = BOOKING`, i.e. "the customer bought two
hours", which then silenced the payroll flag for a shoot whose length nobody
had established.

A number sent WITHOUT this flag is treated as possibly-defaulted and is
dropped when nothing else establishes a length, so an old or cached client
degrades to a flagged shoot rather than to an invented contract. Honoured
values are stamped MANUAL, never BOOKING.

WHO SENDS IT: `JobRequestForm` → `JobManagementContext.createJob` →
`api.projects.create`, and only on the branch where the selected services
carry NO duration of their own — the branch that renders the free-text
"minutes" input. Whatever sits in that input got there by a human act (typed
in, or dragged as a span on the calendar and carried in through
`initialValues`); nothing seeds it, and clearing it leaves it empty. When the
catalogue does answer, the field is read-only and the flag is NOT sent: the
PM's +15m / +30m / +60m top-up is already covered by the longer-than-
catalogue rule, which records the same MANUAL stamp.

(`allowsQuantity: false`) is pinned to 1 here regardless of what arrives.

Normalised server-side by `sanitizeAddOnQuantities`; the client's numbers
are a request, not a fact.

discountId.description:
THE PROMOTIONAL INCENTIVE A COORDINATOR ATTACHES WHILE BOOKING BY HAND.

`JobRequestForm` → `JobManagementContext.createJob` → `api.projects.create`
is the ONLY client, and this is the door the staff "New Project" dialog
actually goes through (not `POST /orders/create`).

An `OrgDiscount` by row id (a named markdown the org configured) or by
coupon `code` — send EXACTLY ONE. Both, or neither, is refused as
`ambiguous_request` and the project is still created.

── NO AMOUNT CROSSES THE WIRE ─────────────────────────────────────────────
Deliberately. The server re-reads the row in THIS org, re-prices it against
the invoice it actually built and clamps it (`priceCoupon`). A client that
could state its own reduction could make any job free.

── DECLARING THEM IS NOT AUTHORIZING THEM ─────────────────────────────────
`BookingIncentivesService.assertMayApplyIncentives` checks
`invoices.discount:write` IN THE ORG BEING BILLED before any of this is
honoured, because a linked agent-customer arrives as PERSONAL_OWNER of
their own org and passes every naive role check. They are declared here
because `ValidationPipe` runs `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` — an undeclared
field is a 400 and therefore NO PROJECT AT ALL, which would turn a coupon
typo into a lost booking.

rewardEntitlementId.description:
A `LoyaltyEntitlement` THE CUSTOMER ALREADY HOLDS, spent on this job.

A reward is not a coupon and is never applied as one: it is a single-use
asset the customer owns, it reduces the TAXABLE BASE (CRA taxes the
discounted price), and it is claimed with a guarded UPDATE before any
credit is derived from it. See `orders/booking-incentives.ts`.

Ownership is re-checked server-side against the booking's customer, so a
coordinator cannot spend one customer's reward on another's job.

sendInvoiceOnCreate.description:
THE PER-JOB "Email the invoice now" SWITCH on the staff New Project dialog.

`true` emails the invoice this booking raises as soon as the project is
created — after any coupon or reward has landed on it. `false` keeps it a
DRAFT for this one job, to be sent by hand or when the job is delivered
(`Organization.sendInvoiceOnDelivery`).

OMIT IT to get the org's own "Send the invoice when an order is placed"
(`Organization.autoSendInvoiceOnOrder`) — which is what every API/MCP caller
and every web build older than the switch gets. It is an override for one
job, never a second billing setting.

Ignored when the booking raises no invoice (no package). Declared here
because `ValidationPipe` runs `forbidNonWhitelisted: true`: an undeclared
key is a 400 and no project at all, so the web client only sends it once
the org payload proves this build knows it (`sendInvoiceOnDelivery` on
`GET /organizations/:id` ships in the same deploy).

STRICTLY A BOOLEAN. The global pipe runs `enableImplicitConversion`, which
turns ANY non-null value into `Boolean(value)` before `@IsBoolean` looks
at it — so the string "false" would arrive as `true` and email a customer
the caller asked us not to. `@IsStrictBoolean` hands the validator the raw
value instead, and anything that is not `true`/`false` is a 400.

contractedDurationMinutes.description:
The shoot's contracted length in minutes. When set, `endTime` is DERIVED
from it (start + duration) so the calendar block and the pay run can never
describe this shoot differently — the two used to be written by separate
code paths, and `contractedDurationMinutes` was never written at all.

Preferred over `endTime` on this route: the webapp's shoot form leaves the
end-time input optional, so extra shoots were routinely created with
neither an end time nor a length.

MUST stay declared: `whitelist: true` silently strips undeclared fields.

The added shoot's contracted length in minutes. When set, `endTime` is
DERIVED from it so the calendar block and the pay run agree by construction.

When neither this nor `endTime` is sent, an `add_items` shoot falls back to
the total duration of the add-ons it is being CHARGED for
(`pricing.addOnIds`) — the length that was actually sold. A `split` shoot
reuses the order's already-purchased items, so nothing implies a length for
it and it is left with none rather than one being invented.

MUST stay declared: `whitelist: true` silently strips undeclared fields.

THE MANUAL DURATION OVERRIDE, in minutes.

A shoot's length is fixed at booking from the package it was sold with (plus
its add-ons) and may thereafter change ONLY through an explicit gesture like
this one. Sending it rewrites `ProjectVisit.contractedDurationMinutes`, marks
the provenance MANUAL, records who changed it, and derives `endTime` from it
so the calendar block and the pay run cannot describe the same shoot
differently.

WHY IT DID NOT EXIST BEFORE: `contractedDurationMinutes` shipped with a doc
comment promising "a reviewer sets it from the pay run", but no DTO carried
it and no route wrote it — the column had ZERO writers in the entire
product. The nearest thing was the optional end-time input, which rewrote a
span with no record that a human had decided anything. Note that
`payrollOnSiteSecondsOverride` is NOT this field: that corrects the MEASURED
on-site time, this one sets the CONTRACT.

`null` clears it back to "not established", which returns the shoot to being
FLAGGED at pay time rather than paying a number nobody stands behind.

THAT SENTENCE IS TRUE ONLY BECAUSE THE WINDOW IS REMOVED WITH THE STAMP.
`endTime` is DERIVED from this field on every write, so it took two rounds
to make the promise real, and the second round is the one worth knowing:

  • Clearing the stamp ALONE left the derived window in place, and
    `resolveShootPaidSeconds` just dropped from precedence 2 to precedence 3
    and re-paid the identical seconds as a `BOOKED_WINDOW` with an empty
    attention array — the operator withdrew the number and nothing
    downstream heard.
  • Clearing it and REPLACING the window with a placeholder-length one was
    worse on a 60-minute package: `packageCorroboratesVisitSpan` vouches for
    a window that equals the package's own duration, which turns off the
    very refusal the placeholder length was chosen to trigger, so
    withdrawing a 45-minute stamp on such an order RAISED the shoot from
    2700 s to 3600 s, still unflagged.

`resolveVisitTimeWrite` now sets `endTime` to NULL when the window was the
cleared stamp's own derivative. The shoot then states no length at all —
nothing at any precedence, and no window for the package to vouch for — so
it is `SHOOT_DURATION_MISSING` for every package duration, which is the
promise above.

Send `endTime` in the SAME request to mean "clear the number but KEEP this
window" — an explicit window is the caller's own statement and is honoured
as-is (still unstamped). That is what the shoot-duration dialog sends when
it can land on the order's package.

Bounded to a day — a longer shoot is a data-entry slip, and an unbounded
value here would be paid.

MUST stay declared: `whitelist: true` silently strips undeclared body fields.

Optional proximity hint for placing the address on the map. Never stored:
the saved coordinates are always geocoded from the address fields.

lng.description: Optional proximity hint; never stored. See `lat`.

returnsHere.description:
Does the technician also RETURN here at the end of the day?

Defaults false: a one-off start from somewhere else still ends at their
real home. True is the multi-day stay out of area. The end-of-day return
leg is measured to whichever this resolves to, so a wrong default here

rather than a global rule.

Either an existing account or an email address. An account joins
immediately; an unknown email is INVITED and joins on accept.

Deliberately NOT `@IsEmail()`. The roster UI can save while someone is
mid-type, and a 400 on a half-typed address is worse than a row that
never resolves — the service lower-cases and looks it up, and an address

OWNER is rejected by the service: ownership is transferred explicitly, not
handed out by adding a second one.

STANDING team role — separate axis from `role` (listing access). Absent =
AGENT (an ordinary teammate). ADMINISTRATOR/ASSISTANT are the managing /
non-managing tiers the portal team offers.

Materialise a real ProjectShare for every order I am CURRENTLY the primary
customer of. Each becomes its own auditable, individually-revocable row —
a standing rule never becomes an implicit predicate.

brokerageLogo.description: A CDN URL from the media presign-general upload flow.

expiresAt.description: Optional auto-expiry. Enforced LIVE by the predicate, not by a cron.

type.description:
The media type CODE this file belongs to. See `GET /media-types` for the
organization's vocabulary — the built-ins plus any `CUSTOM_…` type it
created.

⚠️ `@IsString()` and NOT `@IsEnum(MediaType)`. A validation decorator is
evaluated ONCE at class-definition time, with no request and no
organization in scope, so it cannot know which codes this org defined — and
under `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` an `@IsEnum` here would 400 a
photographer uploading into a lane the org itself created.

The check is not removed, it MOVED to where the org is known:
`MediaService.normalizeMediaType` resolves the org's registry and refuses a

The RAW FOLDER LAYOUT: subfolders created inside every job's Drive folder,
each with the role that decides how its photos are edited.

Omitted = unchanged. `null` or an empty `folders` list = no layout.
Duplicate names (case-insensitive), "/" and the other rules the stored
value must satisfy are checked by the service through
`readRawFolderLayout` — the one reader — and come back as a 400 with its
message.

folder.description:
The parent folder, as either a Drive URL or a bare id. Admins paste the URL
because that is what Drive's Share dialog hands them; the service accepts
both rather than making that a support ticket per org.

enabled.description:
Keep the configuration but stop creating folders. A literal true/false
only: under the pipe's implicit conversion a bare @IsBoolean turns the
string "false" into true — switching Drive ON when the caller said off.

autoDeclineBookings.description:
REMOVED FEATURE — accepted and ignored. Nothing reads this any more.

Auto-decline did two things, both deleted: it removed a technician from the
PUBLIC booking pool entirely (every day, every slot — not just out-of-hours,
which is what the name implied), silently hiding real availability from
customers; and it turned an out-of-hours manual assignment into a hard 409.
The backing column is dropped in the accompanying migration.

The FIELD survives only because validation runs with
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an unknown key 400s the WHOLE request. A
browser tab opened before this shipped still PUTs `autoDeclineBookings`;
removing the field would break saving availability for those sessions.
Safe to delete once stale clients have rolled over.

isCondo.description:
Is this level a condo unit? Per floor, like `isAboveGrade`. A condo
 level's Total RMS is paint-to-paint (RECA RMS Principle 5); its outer-face
 figure is reported only as an additional "not the RMS area" line. Default
 false. Only applied when the floor is CREATED — a row reused by label
 keeps its own value (see `addFloor`). `true` on a property still on the
 older INTERIOR basis is a 409 (`code: CONDO_NEEDS_LEVEL_SWITCH`): that
 property switches to condo-unit levels through `convert-interior-basis`
 (see `assertCondoLevelAllowedOnBasis`).

countsTowardGla.description:
Does this floor count toward Gross Living Area? Default true. Set false
 for unfinished space (e.g. an unfinished basement) to exclude it from GLA
 while it still counts in total/exterior area. Writing it re-runs the
 property area recompute so totals refresh immediately.

isCondo.description:
Is this level a condo unit? Per floor, like `isAboveGrade`. A condo
 level's Total RMS is paint-to-paint (RECA RMS Principle 5); its outer-face
 figure is reported only as an additional "not the RMS area" line. Writing
 it re-runs the property area recompute and marks the delivered plans
 dirty, so both refresh without a canvas edit. Turning it ON for a level
 of a property still on the older INTERIOR basis is a 409
 (`code: CONDO_NEEDS_LEVEL_SWITCH`) and writes nothing: that property
 switches to condo-unit levels through `convert-interior-basis` (see
 `assertCondoLevelAllowedOnBasis`).

interiorWallThicknessInches.description:
Interior partition thickness. Stored inside Floor.layoutJson (not a column) to avoid a
Prisma migration; the service merges this into layoutJson when present.

hidden.description:
Hide / un-hide the floor — see `Floor.hiddenAt`. Stored as a timestamp,
sent as a boolean (matching `TourNode.hidden`, the same concept one grain
down).

MUST stay declared here even though the service routes it to
`setFloorHidden` (which carries a last-visible-floor guard) rather than
writing it as a plain column: the global ValidationPipe runs
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true`, so an UNDECLARED field is rejected with a 400
and a PATCH carrying `{ hidden: true }` would fail as a whole. The dedicated
`PATCH .../floors/:floorId/hidden` route is what the web UI uses; declaring
it here keeps this route usable for every other client.

excludeReason.description:
User-supplied exclusion reason. Stored as free text but the picker
surfaces SUNROOM / UNFINISHED / ATTIC / LOW_CEILING / OTHER. Pass an
empty string to clear (back to auto-derivation).

depthInches.description: Phase 6: BAY/BOW perpendicular protrusion from the wall (in).

outerWidthInches.description: Phase 6: BAY trapezoid outer-wall width (in). NULL for BOW.

depthInches.description: Phase 6: BAY/BOW perpendicular protrusion from the wall (in).

outerWidthInches.description: Phase 6: BAY trapezoid outer-wall width (in). NULL for BOW.

note.description: Why the admin/owner is overriding this event.

syncVisitStatus.description: Also update the shoot's status to match the corrected record. Default true.

effectiveFrom.description: ISO date/time events before this stop counting toward the aggregate. Defaults to now.

note.description: Why the stats are being reset.

visitId.description:
The specific shoot (ProjectVisit) this ping belongs to. Optional for
backward compatibility with clients that predate per-shoot tracking
(Phase 1 crew-reliability), and unavoidable for the 98-of-116 production
projects that have no `ProjectVisit` row at all. Omitting it keeps the
legacy project-level behaviour (keyed on `visitId IS NULL`).

It NO LONGER skips the gates. It used to skip both the assigned-technician
check and the shoot-window check outright, because both lived inside an
`if (visit && …)`. The assigned-technician check now runs on this path too,
against the PROJECT's assignment, and the window check degrades to the
shoot's own local day (a project-level trip has no place in the day's shoot
sequence to be gated against). Passing a visitId still gets the full
per-shoot window, which additionally waits out the technician's previous
same-day shoot.

latitude.description:
Live position of the technician, from `CLLocation.coordinate`.

UNBOUNDED, and validated as a PAIR server-side. `kCLLocationCoordinate2DInvalid`
has both members set to `kCLLocationDegreesInvalid` (`-180.0`) — a legal
longitude and an impossible latitude — so a `@Min(-90)` here would 400 the
phase transition of any client that forwards the sentinel instead of
filtering it. `normalizeCoordinate` records the sentinel, a half pair and
an out-of-range axis all as "no fix", which is treated exactly like sending
no coordinate at all: the last known position stands.

longitude.description: See `latitude` — the pair is normalised together and bounded nowhere.

headingDegrees.description:
Direction of travel in degrees clockwise from due north, from
`CLLocation.course` (or `CLHeading.trueHeading`).

UNBOUNDED, and this one is the sharpest edge on the DTO. Apple documents a
NEGATIVE course as "the direction is invalid", which is the state of a
phone that is STATIONARY — i.e. a technician standing in a driveway about
to start their trip. The `@Min(0)` this field used to carry meant the most
ordinary moment in the whole feature was one client change away from
400ing. `normalizeHeadingDegrees` records a negative course as "direction
unknown", folds `360` to `0`, and refuses to invent a bearing for anything
above that rather than wrapping garbage into a confident lie.

horizontalAccuracy.description:
`CLLocation.horizontalAccuracy` for THIS ping, in metres — the radius of
the 68%-confidence circle around `latitude`/`longitude`.

WHY IT MUST BE DECLARED HERE: the global pipe runs with
`whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true` (main.ts), so an undeclared
key does not merely get dropped — it 400s the WHOLE ping, and every client
in the tree treats a non-2xx trip POST as a retryable failure. Shipping the
field client-side without this declaration would take the technician's
entire trip offline, not degrade one column.

DELIBERATELY UNBOUNDED. CoreLocation reports a NEGATIVE accuracy when the
fix is invalid, and a cell-tower-only fix legitimately reports thousands of
metres. A `@Min(0)`/`@Max(n)` here would turn "my GPS is poor" into "your
trip failed", so the value is accepted as sent and normalised server-side
(negative / non-finite ⇒ stored as null, i.e. "quality unknown").

Persisted to `ProjectTracking.horizontalAccuracyMeters` on every ping, and
to `ProjectTracking.startAccuracyMeters` for the ping that supplies the
trip ORIGIN — payroll bills kilometres against that origin and has to be
able to reject a 3 km cell-tower fix before it does.

etaSeconds.description:
Seconds until estimated arrival at the property, from
`MKRoute.expectedTravelTime`. Passed through so the customer-side UI can
render the same number the tech sees.

UNBOUNDED, AND NOT `@IsInt()`. This is the field that stranded a technician
in a driveway: a wrong device fix produced a genuinely-computed ~97,500 s
route, `@Max(60 * 60 * 24)` rejected it, and the trip could not be started
at all. The source is a `TimeInterval` (Double), so `@IsInt()` was a second
trap waiting on any client that stopped truncating before it serialised.

`normalizeEtaSeconds` rounds to the column's Int, and records anything
beyond a day as `null` — the customer's map then shows no ETA instead of
"1625 min to property" — while LOGGING it, because an absurd ETA is the
best available signal that a device's fix is wrong.

note.description:
Free-text note attached to this ping ("stuck in traffic on
 the 401"). Surfaced verbatim to the customer.

action.description:
`COMPLETE` — assert the trip finished. Requires {@link completedAt} UNLESS
the row already has a device-recorded `phaseTimestamps.COMPLETE`.
`CANCEL`   — end the live state without asserting the technician arrived
             or worked. Never writes a completion timestamp.

completedAt.description:
The ACTUAL instant the technician finished, ISO-8601. Required for
`COMPLETE` when the trip never recorded its own completion, because
payroll derives on-site seconds from ARRIVED → COMPLETE — the server
refuses to invent this value. Ignored for `CANCEL`, and ignored for
`COMPLETE` on a row that already has a device-recorded completion (that
timestamp is reused verbatim).

note.description: Free-text reason, recorded on the audit-log entry alongside the actor.

orgId.description:
The org the lead is FOR — the company whose public mini-site the form sits
on. Required: every read of a lead (the org's /leads inbox, iOS, the
portal) is scoped by `Inquiry.orgId`, so a lead written without one is
stored and then never shown to anybody. It must name an org the public
mini-site would render (`findPublicOrgOrThrow`); anything else is a 404,
not a write.

type.description:
WHY A TRANSFORM SITS IN FRONT OF THE ENUM.

OrgType.TEAM was renamed to BROKERAGE on 2026-09-19 so that the org SHAPE
and the new OrgSubscriptionPlan.TEAM could not be confused on the same row.
The webapp creates brokerage orgs by posting {"type":"TEAM"}, and a browser
holding pre-rename JS will keep doing so for as long as its bundle is
cached. Without this coercion that request fails @IsEnum and an agent
cannot create their team — a deploy-order bug, not a validation success.

The transform runs BEFORE validation, so the legacy spelling is normalised
rather than rejected. Delete it once no client sends 'TEAM'.

logoUrl.description: Optional branding logo (a CDN URL) set at creation — used by agent team orgs.

editorMediaTypes.description:
WHICH MEDIA TYPES THIS PERSON IS BEING ONBOARDED FOR. Copied onto
`OrganizationMember.editorMediaTypes` when the invite is accepted, and
ignored entirely for a CUSTOMER invite.

IT EXISTS BECAUSE THE RULE SAYS "FROM THE MOMENT THEY'RE ONBOARDED". A media
type may be marked complete only by somebody classified for it and staffed
on the job; until 2026-09-13 the only place to state a classification was
one team page per person, after the fact. That is fine for a policy nobody
reads and fatal for one that decides whether a new hire's first job has a
Complete button anybody can press.

OMITTING IT NOW MEANS THEY COVER NOTHING — CHANGED 2026-09-20. This used to
say "omit it and nothing breaks: an invited TECHNICIAN or EDITOR still gets
the lane their role implies". No role implies a lane any more
(`isClassifiedFor`, sla/completion-policy.ts): "No specialty selection
doesn't mean 'all'." A person invited without this field can be staffed on
jobs and cannot mark any media type complete until somebody ticks one, on
this route or on their Team page.

So SEND IT for anybody who finishes work — the photographer closing out
their own photos as much as the TECHNICIAN who also drafts floor plans or
the ASSISTANT-carried contractor who does the tours. The org's enforcement
window (`Organization.deliverableCompletionEnforcedFrom`) is what stops an
omission biting on day one, and the org's settings screen lists everybody
an omission has left uncovered.

REQUIRED FOR AN `EDITOR` INVITE SINCE 2026-09-22, and the owner was asked
about this route by name: "It should be a requirement that an editor has a
specialisation … Even on team invite." An EDITOR arriving with nothing
ticked is a title that says "this person does the editing" over a record
that says they cover nothing — unroutable and unable to mark anything
complete. Every other role may still omit it.

⚠️ STILL `@IsOptional()`, AND THE REQUIREMENT IS ENFORCED IN THE SERVICE —
two reasons, either sufficient:

  1. The check is about EMPTINESS AFTER NORMALISATION, and normalisation
     needs the org's media-type registry (see the note below). A body of
     `['PHTOO']` is a non-empty array that this org has no lane for; it
     normalises to nothing and must be refused exactly like `[]`. No
     decorator can know that.
  2. `@IsOptional()` and `@ValidateIf(...)` are the SAME mechanism in
     class-validator — both register a conditional, and validation is
     skipped when ANY of them says so. So a naive
     `@ValidateIf(o => o.role === 'EDITOR') @ArrayNotEmpty()` bolted on
     beside `@IsOptional()` silently never fires on the omission case,
     which is the case it was added for.

`OrganizationsService.createInvite` is the authority — see
`common/editor-classification.util.ts`.

MEDIA-TYPE CODES, not `MediaType` enum members — an org defines its own
types (`CUSTOM_TWILIGHT`), and the live vocabulary is `GET /media-types`.

⚠️ `@IsString({ each: true })` and NOT `@IsEnum(MediaType, { each: true })`,
and this is the same trade every media-type field in the API now makes. A
decorator is evaluated ONCE, at class-definition time, with no request and
no organization in scope, so it cannot possibly know this org's codes — and
under `forbidNonWhitelisted: true` an `@IsEnum` here would 400 an org's own
custom lane rather than silently drop it. The check has not been removed, it
MOVED to the service, where the org IS known: `normalizeSpecialties` is
called with that org's registry, so a code this org does not have is still
refused.

WHICH MEDIA TYPES EVERY REDEEMER OF THIS CODE IS CLASSIFIED FOR — the same
field `CreateInviteDto` carries, for the reusable-link version of the same
act. Copied onto `Invitation.editorMediaTypes` and from there onto each
`OrganizationMember` the code mints, and ignored entirely for a CUSTOMER
code.

REQUIRED WHEN `role` IS `EDITOR`, enforced in
`OrganizationsService.createInviteCode` for the reasons spelled out on
`CreateInviteDto.editorMediaTypes` (normalisation needs the org's registry,
and `@IsOptional()` would swallow a `@ValidateIf` requirement on the
omission case). A code is a reusable invite, so leaving it unguarded would
be the hole a second entry point always is — and worse than the single
invite, because it mints an unclassified editor for every person who ever
redeems it and leaves no one address for an admin to notice afterwards.

MEDIA-TYPE CODES, not `MediaType` enum members: an org defines its own
(`CUSTOM_TWILIGHT`), the live vocabulary is `GET /media-types`, and a code
this org does not have is dropped by `normalizeSpecialties` in the service
rather than 400ed by a decorator that cannot see the organization.

granted.description: True when this org may use the feature. The union of its plan grants and its active add-on subscriptions.

limit.description: Maximum quantity this org may hold. ABSENT means unlimited — do not read an absent field as zero.

customEmailDomain.description: Granted when the org may use "Custom email domain".

customAppDomain.description: Granted when the org may use "Custom domains (white-label)".

brochures.description: Granted when the org may use "Brochure generation".

whitelabelApp.description: Granted when the org may use "Branded mobile app". Unlike the others this one is CAPPED (limit 1): each branded app costs a bundle id, an Apple Developer slot, CI minutes and a human review, so it is the one entitlement with real marginal cost per tenant.

plan.description: Plan label for display. FOUNDER wins over ENTERPRISE when both apply — it names the arrangement, while isEnterprise names the access.

isEnterprise.description: True when the org holds the ENTERPRISE (or FOUNDER) plan AND is paying. This is the PLAN question, not a feature question: an active add-on SKU grants a feature to an org that reads false here, so clients must gate on features[key].granted, never on this.

subscriptionActive.description: Enterprise AND actually paying (active / trialing / past_due, a card-less granted trial, or FOUNDER). False for a lapsed enterprise, which keeps every feature but falls back to the per-transaction fee.

transactionFeePct.description: The percentage a charge would actually take right now: 0 when exempt, otherwise the effective rate including any per-org override. Measured through computePlatformFeeCents, so it cannot disagree with what Stripe takes. Always a number on the wire; null is reserved for clients modelling "not loaded yet".

canUseOwnStripeAccount.description: True when this org may install its own Stripe credentials and switch its payments off Stripe Connect — a paid-tier privilege (Teams, Enterprise, Founder, or a staff override). Clients MUST gate the "bring your own Stripe account" control on this rather than on transactionFeePct === 0: a paid org that has not switched over yet still pays the percentage, so deriving it from the fee hides the control from precisely the org that needs it. Pair the two — this one answers "may you leave Connect", transactionFeePct answers "have you".

features.description: One { granted, limit? } per gated feature — the union of the plan grants and any active add-on SKU subscriptions. Clients gate the UI on these so a Free org is shown an upgrade path instead of a button that 403s. Gate on `granted`, never on which SKU was sold: SKUs are repriced and rebundled, entitlement keys are not.

slug.description:
═══ THIS FIELD IS A DNS LABEL, NOT A DISPLAY STRING ══════════════════════

It becomes `<slug>.vremly.com`, which `registerSubdomain` /
`removeSubdomain` interpolate into a Vercel management-API URL PATH. As a
bare `@IsString()` it accepted `../../../../v9/projects/<projectId>#`,
which a URL parser resolves to `/v9/projects/<projectId>` — on the DELETE,
that is "delete the entire Vercel project", carrying VERCEL_API_TOKEN, and
it takes vremly.com and app.vremly.com down together. Reachable by any
authenticated user: create a COMPANY org (you become OWNER), PATCH the slug
to arm it, PATCH again so `slugChanged` fires the teardown.

`@Matches` is the SOURCE half of that fix. `assertProvisionableHost` at
every outbound Vercel URL is the sink half, and neither assumes the other
ran. Reserved-name screening is applied in the service, against the SAME
exported list `generateUniqueSlug` uses on create — see org-slug.ts.

`@MaxLength` is redundant against the pattern and kept anyway: a length
violation reports as a length violation, which is what the person renaming
their company actually needs to be told.

sessionRecordingEnabled.description:
The org's own switch for third-party session recording (Microsoft
Clarity). False stops the recorder for this organisation's staff AND its
portal customers, everywhere, without a deploy — see
Organization.sessionRecordingEnabled in schema.prisma and the fourth gate
in components/shared/analytics/ClarityInit.tsx.

Sits next to the legal links deliberately: the person editing an
organisation's terms and privacy URLs is the person who needs to find it.

smsNumber.description: The Twilio SENDING number. Nobody reads replies to it.

supportTextNumber.description:
The number CUSTOMERS may text — shown as a "Text" button on the portal,
the delivery page, iOS and email footers. Empty string clears it.

lat.description:
Optional proximity hint for placing the address on the map. Never stored:
the saved coordinates are always geocoded from the address fields.

lng.description: Optional proximity hint; never stored. See `lat`.

videoScriptDefaultLengthSeconds.description:
═══ THE COMPANY'S HOUSE STYLE FOR AI VIDEO SCRIPTS ══════════════════════

The five script controls, set ONCE for the company instead of re-picked on
every generation: length, tone, pace, what the hook leads with, and how far
the writing may depart from a literal description. A per-generation request
overrides any of them individually — the resolution order is REQUEST →
THESE → the built-in, PER FIELD, in `resolveScriptControls`.

THIS IS THE ONLY WRITE PATH THEY HAVE, and it is the reason they are here
rather than only on the generate request. The ORDER-TRIGGERED generation
has no user to ask — it fires from an order-creation hook or a sweep tick —
so it resolves against these columns and nothing else. Without a route a
company that shoots luxury listings could set its house style only through
a psql session, which is how `allowCustomerWebsiteEdits` above spent months
pinned to its default.

`@IsIn` AGAINST THE SHARED ALLOWLISTS, imported rather than restated. These
values are INTERPOLATED INTO AN LLM SYSTEM PROMPT, so the set of legal
strings has exactly one definition (`video-script-controls.ts`) and a
second copy here is how a value this route accepts stops being a value the
prompt understands. Out of range is a 400, never a coercion — and
`resolveScriptControls` checks these columns AGAIN when it reads them, so a
value written by a restored backup still cannot reach the model.

NULL IS MEANINGFUL AND STAYS REACHABLE: it means "this company never chose
one", which is a different fact from "chose the same thing the built-in
says" and stays different if a built-in is ever changed. `@ValidateIf`
admits an explicit `null` so a company can clear a choice; `@IsOptional`
alone would make `null` a validation error and leave no way back.

videoScriptDefaultBoldness.description:
safe | balanced | bold. IT IS NOT A TEMPERATURE SETTING and must never be
made into one — see the docblock on `SCRIPT_BOLDNESS`. It changes the
instruction language the model is given; grounding is absolute at every
value, including `bold`.

allowCustomerWebsiteEdits.description:
"May the listing agent edit their own delivered property website?"

ADDED 2026-08-13. The column has existed and been ENFORCED since the
customer-website-editing work (`listings.service.ts` refuses the edit when
it is false), but it was in no DTO and on no route — the only way to switch
it off was a psql session, and every org therefore ran on the `true`
default. Locking it down per listing
(`ListingWebsiteConfig.customerEditsLockedAt`) was the only reachable
substitute, one listing at a time.

Deliberately NOT given a new default here: the column stays
`@default(true)`, so declaring it changes nothing until somebody flips it.

paymentRoutingMode.description:
HOW this org's customer payments move. OPERATIONAL ONLY.

It does NOT and MUST NOT decide whether the platform charges its fee.
That is `computePlatformFeeCents` (common/plans.ts), which reads the org's
plan and exemptions — never a preference the org sets about itself. Until
2026-08-29 `DIRECT_STRIPE` dropped `application_fee_amount` in all three
charge paths, so this one field was a self-serve waiver of the 3%: the org
kept `transfer_data.destination` (100% of the money) and paid nothing.

`DIRECT_STRIPE` additionally requires staff to have provisioned real
direct settlement (`stripeDirectCharges` / `stripeStandaloneMode`, neither
of which is in this DTO); the service 403s otherwise.

captureStrategy.description:
WHEN THE CUSTOMER'S CARD IS CHARGED at booking checkout.

  IMMEDIATE    — charge at checkout.
  MANUAL_LATER — authorize at checkout; someone captures on delivery via
                 `POST /orders/:projectId/capture`. THE DEFAULT, and the
                 behaviour every checkout had hardcoded before this setting

declared field here — under `forbidNonWhitelisted` a brand-new field would

When true, an order with no `scheduledTime` counts as REQUESTED scheduling

applyLoyaltyCredits.description:
Loyalty credits the customer wants spent on this order — the SAME two
fields `CreateOrderDto` carries, so the quote can be asked the same
question the checkout will be asked.

They were missing here, and that was the original hole: the checkout paths
have always deducted credits from the Stripe amount
(`chargeableFromCheckoutTax(checkoutTax, creditsAppliedCents)`) while
`grossTotalCents` — documented as "exactly what the card will be charged" —
could not even see them. A customer with credits was quoted one number and
charged a smaller one. Smaller is not harmless: the confirm screen is the
only place the reduction is visible, so a credit balance silently
evaporated with nothing on screen saying it had been spent.

redeemEntitlementId.description:
LoyaltyEntitlement the customer intends to redeem on this order.

Quoting NEVER reserves and never spends — this route creates nothing. It
answers one question: if this reward were applied to this exact cart, what
would the card be charged, and if it could NOT be applied, why not. The
"why not" is the point: a `free_package` reward is 100% off the MATCHING
package's line, so a cart that does not contain that package cannot use it.
Returning it as inapplicable-with-a-reason is the whole contract —
silently pricing it at zero would show the customer a reward they still
hold as though they had just spent it.

so the anonymous booking portal can price a cart, and `JwtAuthGuard`
populates `req.user` best-effort there; with no caller the reward comes
back `requires_sign_in` rather than being priced. The unauthenticated
booking flow cannot redeem, by design.

the public page advertised it with "Included with this booking. It is
applied automatically, with nothing to enter" — while this endpoint, which
produces the only total the customer ever sees, was never told which form
they had arrived through. It could not price the offer even in principle,
so the review screen showed full list price under a banner promising the
opposite, and the invoice then charged that full price.

Quoting NEVER claims. The slot is taken at submission, so an abandoned cart
cannot burn a claim out of a capped campaign.

the same contract `GET /booking-forms/public/:id/promotion` already uses

── WHAT THE CLIENT DOES NOT GET TO DECIDE ─────────────────────────────────
Neither field carries an AMOUNT, deliberately. The server re-reads the
`OrgDiscount` row in the PROVIDER's org, re-prices it against the invoice
it actually built, and clamps it — see `priceCoupon`. A client that could
name its own reduction would be a client that could make any order free.

── AND WHO GETS TO SEND THEM ──────────────────────────────────────────────
`POST /orders/create` is reachable by customers, so declaring these on the
DTO does NOT authorize them: `BookingIncentivesService.assertMayApplyIncentives`
checks `invoices.discount:write` IN THE PROVIDER ORG before either is
honoured. They are declared here because `ValidationPipe` runs
`forbidNonWhitelisted: true` — an undeclared field is a 400, which would
make a coordinator's coupon look like a broken booking.

── AND WHICH ROUTES CAN ACTUALLY SETTLE ONE ───────────────────────────────
ONLY the doors that raise an INVOICE: `POST /orders/create` on its
invoice-after-delivery branch, and the staff New Project door. A coupon is
a flat post-tax snapshot off a taxed invoice, and the card-at-checkout
routes (`POST /orders/checkout`, `POST /orders/native-checkout`, and
`POST /orders/create` when the provider org requires upfront payment)
charge before any invoice exists. Those routes REFUSE these two fields
with a 400 rather than ignoring them — see
`OrdersService.assertCheckoutCannotCarryCoupon`. `redeemEntitlementId`
above is different and IS honoured there, because a reward reduces the
cart's taxable base before the charge.

Explicit approval of the exact preview, including creation and provider notification effects.

mediaIds.description: One to six visible finished photos to assess. Drafts only assess these selected artifacts, never the person overall.

confirmed.description: Explicit approval of the reviewed evidence and submitted grades
